# dgetsqrhrt

> Computes a column-blocked QR factorization of a real `M`-by-`N` matrix `A` (with `M >= N`) via TSQR followed by Householder reconstruction.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dgetsqrhrt from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dgetsqrhrt';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dgetsqrhrt( order, M, N, mb1, nb1, nb2, A, LDA, T, LDT, WORK ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout (`'row-major'` or `'column-major'`) |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of rows of the matrix `A` (`M >= N`)<br>Requires `M ≥ 0` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns of the matrix `A`<br>Rejects `N < 0 \|\| M < N` |
| `mb1` | `integer` | TSQR row block size (`mb1 > N`)<br>Rejects `mb1 <= N` |
| `nb1` | `integer` | TSQR column block size (`nb1 >= 1`)<br>Rejects `nb1 < 1` |
| `nb2` | `integer` | HRT (output) block size (`nb2 >= 1`)<br>Rejects `nb2 < 1` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A`<br>Column-major requires `LDA ≥ max(1, M)`<br>Row-major requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `T` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>min(nb2, N) × N</sub> | **out** · Output `nb2`-by-`N` matrix of upper triangular block reflectors |
| ↳ `LDT` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `T`<br>Column-major requires `LDT ≥ max(1, min(nb2, N))`<br>Row-major requires `LDT ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ MAX(1,LWORKOPT)</sub> | **out** · Workspace array |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix A. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix A. $M \ge N \ge 0$.
- `mb1`: The row block size to be used in the blocked TSQR. $\mathrm{MB1} > N$.
- `nb1`: The column block size to be used in the blocked TSQR. $N \ge \mathrm{NB1} \ge 1$.
- `nb2`: The block size to be used in the blocked QR that is output. $\mathrm{NB2} \ge 1$.
- `A`: On entry: an M-by-N matrix A.

  On exit: a) the elements on and above the diagonal

  -   of the array contain the N-by-N upper-triangular
  -   matrix R corresponding to the Householder QR;

  b) the elements below the diagonal represent Q by

  the columns of blocked V (compact WY-representation).
- `T`: The upper triangular block reflectors stored in compact form as a sequence of upper triangular blocks.
- `WORK`: (workspace) DOUBLE PRECISION array, dimension (MAX(1,`LWORK`)) On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (`0` = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` third argument is invalid (rejected when `N < 0 \|\| M < N`)
- `RangeError` fourth argument is invalid (rejected when `mb1 <= N`)
- `RangeError` fifth argument is invalid (rejected when `nb1 < 1`)
- `RangeError` sixth argument is invalid (rejected when `nb2 < 1`)
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, M )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` tenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, min( nb2, N ) )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` tenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` `LDA` must be valid for the chosen order
- `RangeError` `LDT` must be valid for the chosen order

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dgetsqrhrt.strided(
    M, N,
    mb1, nb1, nb2,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    T, strideT1, strideT2, offsetT,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of rows of the matrix `A` (`M >= N`)<br>Requires `M ≥ 0` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns of the matrix `A`<br>Rejects `N < 0 \|\| M < N` |
| `mb1` | `integer` | TSQR row block size (`mb1 > N`)<br>Rejects `mb1 <= N` |
| `nb1` | `integer` | TSQR column block size (`nb1 >= 1`)<br>Rejects `nb1 < 1` |
| `nb2` | `integer` | HRT (output) block size (`nb2 >= 1`)<br>Rejects `nb2 < 1` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output matrix |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `A` |
| `T` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>min(nb2, N) × N</sub> | **out** · Output matrix of upper triangular block reflectors |
| ↳ `strideT1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `T` |
| ↳ `strideT2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `T` |
| ↳ `offsetT` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `T` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ MAX(1,LWORKOPT)</sub> | **out** · Workspace array |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride length for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `WORK` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix A. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix A. $M \ge N \ge 0$.
- `mb1`: The row block size to be used in the blocked TSQR. $\mathrm{MB1} > N$.
- `nb1`: The column block size to be used in the blocked TSQR. $N \ge \mathrm{NB1} \ge 1$.
- `nb2`: The block size to be used in the blocked QR that is output. $\mathrm{NB2} \ge 1$.
- `A`: On entry: an M-by-N matrix A.

  On exit: a) the elements on and above the diagonal

  -   of the array contain the N-by-N upper-triangular
  -   matrix R corresponding to the Householder QR;

  b) the elements below the diagonal represent Q by

  the columns of blocked V (compact WY-representation).
- `T`: The upper triangular block reflectors stored in compact form as a sequence of upper triangular blocks.
- `WORK`: (workspace) DOUBLE PRECISION array, dimension (MAX(1,`LWORK`)) On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (`0` = success)

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` second argument is invalid (rejected when `N < 0 \|\| M < N`)
- `RangeError` third argument is invalid (rejected when `mb1 <= N`)
- `RangeError` fourth argument is invalid (rejected when `nb1 < 1`)
- `RangeError` fifth argument is invalid (rejected when `nb2 < 1`)

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `min( M, N ) === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dgetsqrhrt from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dgetsqrhrt';

const M = 8;
const N = 3;
const mb1 = 4;
const nb1 = 2;
const nb2 = 2;
const nb2local = Math.min( nb2, N );
const A = new Float64Array( M * N );
const T = new Float64Array( nb2local * N );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 256 );
let i, j;

// Build a deterministic input matrix (column-major, M-by-N).
for ( j = 0; j < N; j++ ) {
	for ( i = 0; i < M; i++ ) {
		A[ i + ( j * M ) ] = Math.sin( ( i + 1 ) + ( 3 * ( j + 1 ) ) ) + 0.5;
		if ( i === j ) {
			A[ i + ( j * M ) ] += 4.0;
		}
	}
}

const info = dgetsqrhrt( 'column-major', M, N, mb1, nb1, nb2, A, M, T, nb2local, WORK );
console.log( 'INFO = ' + info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'A (R in upper triangle, V below) = ' ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( A ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'T = ' ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( T ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DGETSQRHRT`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DGETSQRHRT computes a `NB2`-sized column blocked QR-factorization of a real M-by-N matrix A with $M \ge N$,

$$
A = Q \, R
$$

The routine uses internally a `NB1`-sized column blocked and `MB1`-sized row blocked TSQR-factorization and perfors the reconstruction of the Householder vectors from the TSQR output. The routine also converts the R\_tsqr factor from the TSQR-factorization output into the R factor that corresponds to the Householder QR-factorization,

A = Q\_tsqr \* R\_tsqr = $Q \, R$.

The output Q and R factors are stored in the same format as in DGEQRT (Q is in blocked compact WY-representation). See the documentation of DGEQRT for more details on the format.

</section>
